ideas.title: Keyhold
ideas.rationale: Ownership is encoded purely in mating tooth geometry (1-tooth vs 2-tooth families, 4mm proud/deep) sitting on a genuinely stepped 7x7 pedestal waffle, giving real part-family variety and a tight fit tolerance (0.4mm) that puts actual interlock risk on the table rather than a cosmetic pass/fail; the render already shows chunky, legible puzzle-key geometry rather than flat plates.

ideas.title: Twin Deck Solitaire
ideas.rationale: A real two-story assembly -- two boards held on posts with a 30mm open air gap and 33 vertically-aligned transfer channels at 1mm tolerance -- is a genuine structural bet with print-fusion and alignment risk, even though the individual part vocabulary (crosses, plain pegs, plain posts) is the least varied of the three ideas.

ideas.title: Eclipse
ideas.rationale: The dome/dish relief pair is a clean literal translation of Othello's flip but the object is otherwise the flattest of the three -- one flat slab, one socket shape, one disc shape read two ways -- and the render reads as a repetitive grid of shallow bumps and dishes with little silhouette variety beyond that single relief motif.
